verdict.rationale: Codex is itself an AI coding agent. Its docs explicitly support delegating tasks: "Delegate a longer task and return when it is ready," running tasks in parallel cloud environments started from the web, GitHub, Linear or Slack, and handing focused work to subagents from the CLI. Hands-on community reports corroborate real delegated work, but reports on reliability are mixed. Missing for 10: consistent independent corroboration that delegated tasks complete reliably.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: Delegate a longer task and return when it is ready.
Run tasks in isolated cloud environments, work in parallel, and start work from the web, GitHub, GitLab, Linear, or Slack.
Ask Codex to delegate focused work to specialized agents, then bring their findings back into the main terminal session.
Inspect the summary and diff, request a follow-up, or open a pull request when the result is ready.
overall it's no worse than having average L3-L4 engs at your disposal
